title: Colosseum: arena of an empire
voices: MyCast two hosts: A = Charon, B = Kore (mycast.gemini_tts_pcm)

lines.text: Hi! This is a MyCast demo, and we are in Rome, next to the Colosseum.
The largest amphitheatre ever built in the ancient world. Who built it?
Emperor Vespasian started construction around AD 72, and his son Titus completed it in AD 80. Later Domitian modified it further.
All three were Flavians, which is why scholars call it the Flavian Amphitheatre.
Exactly. The name Colosseum came later, most likely from a colossal bronze statue of Nero that stood nearby.
How many people did it hold?
An estimated fifty to eighty thousand spectators. It was built of travertine, tuff and Roman concrete.
Gladiator fights, animal hunts, executions, dramas based on myths, and even, briefly, mock sea battles.
Sea battles in the middle of a city sounds incredible. When did it all stop?
The shows ended in the early Middle Ages. Later the Colosseum served as housing, workshops, a fortress and even a quarry.
So Romans took it apart for building stone?
They did, and earthquakes damaged it too. Yet it is still the symbol of Imperial Rome, and it appears on the Italian five euro cent coin.
Next time you hold that coin, think of eighty thousand spectators.
That was a MyCast demo episode. You can build your own podcast at mycast.pro.
